q1: SELECT beer, MAX(price) - MIN(price) AS price_gap, AVG(price) AS avg_price FROM serves WHERE beer IN (SELECT s.beer FROM serves AS s, frequents AS f WHERE s.bar = f.bar AND f.drinker LIKE 'B%' GROUP BY s.beer HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT s.bar) >= 2) GROUP BY beer ORDER BY beer
q2: SELECT s.beer, MAX(s.price) - MIN(s.price) AS price_gap, AVG(s.price) AS avg_price FROM Serves AS s JOIN Frequents AS f ON s.bar = f.bar JOIN Drinker AS d ON f.drinker = d.name WHERE d.name LIKE 'B%' GROUP BY s.beer HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT s.bar) >= 2

Q2, on the other hand, directly joins the Serves, Frequents, and Drinker tables to achieve the same goal, which might lead to different results if the join conditions or the way the data is filtered are not handled correctly.
